quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x725, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Let's see... Hmm... Oh, looks like you each have enough points to choose one final skill.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You've all picked such classic skills! It's fine to go a little bit out of the box, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: (...Why do I get the feeling she's getting ready to cause trouble...)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: For example... This one here! "Summon"! Doesn't it sound super mysterious and cool?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, I saw that one just now as well. The description says... "This skill can be used under certain circumstances to summon characters or creatures that fit the script's worldbuilding rules."

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The script's worldbuilding rules, huh... But, how are we supposed to know what a Marechaussee Hunter can summon?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That's not for us to worry about, my friend! Just learn the skills that interest you, and the GM will take care of the rest!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, you've convinced Paimon... Let's learn "Summon," then! Paimon can't wait to see what kind of thing shows up.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...Well, now that everyone's more or less finished creating their characters, we can begin.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Since two of our players are doing this for the first time, though, let me ask...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Would you like to play on "easy mode," or "authentic mode"?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, what's the difference between the two?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Well, in roleplaying games, the story sometimes changes based on the decisions of the players and the results of the Fateometer.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: For example, if you "fail" a check, that means you cannot use the target skill in that scenario. A "critical failure" may even result in further negative consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: If you choose to play in "authentic mode," every time you elect to use a skill, you'll need to use the Fateometer to see whether you succeed or fail, and face any consequences that may follow.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: If you choose "easy mode" instead, every check will be successful by default, and you won't have to worry about luck playing a factor.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmm... Given that I'd like to focus on the story, I suppose I should pick "easy mode." I'd feel bad if I brought the team down by failing my checks...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? C'mon, don't worry about that! RNG is the lifeblood of roleplaying games! I'm going with "authentic mode" for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Never knowing what you might have to overcome... Doesn't that sound exciting?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Um... I—I'd rather be mentally prepared for what might happen...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Alright. Then I'll mark down Furina for "easy mode." All her checks will be successful by default. As usual, Navia and Lyney will play on "authentic mode."

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What about you, dear partner? How would you like to play?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Are you sure?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Mhm, no need to worry about the pesky Fateometer. Pretty good choice if you just want to relax and play the game.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Honestly, I don't think Clorinde would make things too difficult for us no matter what the Fateometer says... Isn't that right, Clorinde?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: No promises.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... That wasn't super reassuring!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, anyway, enough talk! Let's get started! I want to experience at least a good chunk of the story today.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Speaking of the story... Why is the beginning scene on a beach?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Well, that's because...

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: A long time ago, back when human civilization was still in its infancy, powerful demons and evil sorcerers ruled over the land. They created a host of monsters and sent them to slaughter all humans in existence...

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: Soon, a group of human rebels banded together. With their swords raised, they swore to brave the darkness and, in doing so, subdue each and every monster that sought their destruction. They became known as the Marechaussee Hunters...

choices.text: Let me think about this some more...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Take your time. There's no rush.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Are you sure?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, trust me. You'll see the beauty of RNG!

choices.text: Let me think about this some more...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Take your time. There's no rush.

talks.objective: Listen to Game Master Clorinde's narration

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You open your envelopes at the same time. The message reads...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: "To the honorable and trustworthy Marechaussee Hunters: our kingdom is currently facing a grave crisis."

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: "The lands outside the capital have been overtaken by monsters, and our people are being led astray by forces of wickedness. We beseech you, please help us resolve this crisis, and return peace and stability to our home."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, the layout of this city looks super familiar... It kind of reminds Paimon of Mondstadt!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The script writer must have used a real-world city as a reference when coming up with the map.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Ahem... As experienced Hunters, the layout of the city reminds you of places once traveled. You recall the sight of tree-lined streets and the gentle tranquility of days gone by...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Yet, as you regard the city in front of you, it appears to be little more than an empty shell. Its hollow gates are open to you, beckoning you to come forth and bring salvation back to the town.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I carefully read every line of the letter and turn my attention to the signatures at the bottom. Who issued this commission to us?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You see a long string of unfamiliar names. It would seem that many of the residents of the city issued this commission together. They sensed that things were not right within the kingdom and sent a distress signal to the outside world.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmm, in that case, why don't we take a walk around the city, and see if we can learn anything from the local residents?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Good idea! We might be able to get some leads on the monsters and bad guys we're after!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You look up and see a tavern nearby. It appears to be open for the day.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Why don't we go check out that tavern? If the novels I've read are anything to go by, taverns are usually full of information.

talks.objective: Gather information at the tavern in the capital

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: What? A critical success? Your luck is through the roof today....

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you begin to survey the man's condition, you're immediately able to see past the crude dressing on his leg and assess the inside of his wound.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You've seen many such injuries before. If not properly treated, the man will likely fall victim to serious illness for the rest of his life.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Seeing your serious expression, the man's brow begins to furrow.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm a doctor by trade — please let me redress your wound. You don't have to suffer like this.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You apply a poultice of specialized medicine to the gash, and carefully redress the wound. The man regards you first with bewilderment and then with guilt.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Thank you, friend. I'm sorry for misjudging you earlier. Please accept my apology.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it! That misunderstanding is all in the past now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, do you know where we can find the monsters? We're here to defeat them.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He informs you of the locations of the monsters, and a glimmer of hope returns to his eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Those monsters aren't easy to deal with. Our soldiers are too young to be of much help, and now I'm out of commission as well...

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: But... But if the legendary Marechaussee Hunters are prepared to lend us their strength, then perhaps there's still a chance to turn the tides, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Just take it easy and leave the monsters to us! Fighting them is what we do.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I'll place my trust in you, then. You have my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I just hope all the guards will be able to come back to their families alive. I wish you the best of luck.

talks.objective: Talk to the Melancholic Young Woman

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? A critical success!?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You remain silent as you prepare a pot and fire to use for cooking. The woman stares at you with her mouth agape as you skillfully cut the ingredients and toss them into the pot.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As the soup gently simmers, steam rises from the pot and a hearty aroma begins to fill the air. All trace of sadness is wiped from the woman's expression, replaced by a look of barely-suppressed anticipation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please have some food. Who knows, maybe you'll feel better after eating something delicious?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Ah... Thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: This is the best meal I've had in a long time... probably since my husband left to fight the monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is your husband a Marechaussee Hunter, too?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: A Marechaussee Hunter? No... My husband is just one of the guards from the capital.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: A horde of monsters suddenly appeared near the capital recently, so all the guards were dispatched to fight them.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Do you remember when those monsters appeared?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: ...I'm not completely sure. All I know is that my husband was dispatched to fight them three days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Do you know where he was sent?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: It all happened so fast. When we said our goodbyes, he couldn't even tell me where they were sending him.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll find him! Just try to remain optimistic and wait for good news!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And don't forget to eat.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Thank you all so much. And I will... I will...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah, a critical failure. Unlucky timing...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The captain of the guards reluctantly allows you to assess his condition. Right as you're trying to get a closer look at his leg, your hand slips, and collides against his wound with great force...

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: ARGH!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds like it hurt...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... My skills are a little rusty.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The captain recoils and takes a half step back. He stares down at you, panting heavily, his eyes full of anger.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I don't care what you have to say, or why you're here. You are not welcome in this city.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Get out of my sight. Now!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I understand that you're upset, sir! We'll leave soon, I promise. It's just, if we don't know where to find the monsters, we won't even know where to go...

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Hah, don't tell me you're actually considering fighting one of those things?

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: You know, put any other group of young people in your place, and I might have tried to stop them, but since you're the ones asking...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He informs you of the locations of the monsters with a disdainful tone, as if he's certain you have no chance of making it out alive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, that was scary... Paimon was worried that critical failure meant we weren't gonna learn anything!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to Clorinde's quick thinking!

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Well, are you leaving or not?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We're leaving, we're leaving！

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Although he doesn't seem very... friendly, merchants are usually a good source of information, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Pardon me, sir. I'd like to ask a question, if I may.

dialogues.speaker: Gruff Merchant
dialogues.text: That depends. How much are you willing to pay?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: How about... this much?

dialogues.speaker: Gruff Merchant
dialogues.text: Tch, what do you take me for, some lowly beggar? You can't even buy half an onion with that amount!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Surely an onion can't be that expensive... right?

dialogues.speaker: Gruff Merchant
dialogues.text: What do you know? War is nearly upon us. Everything costs several times what it did before! If you're not gonna buy anything, then scram.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what a nasty guy. Maybe we shouldn't even bother talking to him...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #But he still might have information we need. {NICKNAME}, can you think of something?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sir, we came to this city to solve the very problem you seem to be referring to. The "war" you mentioned... would it happen to be against the monsters outside the city?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If you happen to be well-informed, and know a thing or two about what's going on, we'd appreciate it if you could share that information with us. After all, the sooner this problem gets resolved, the easier it will be for you to do your business.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Hmph. Well, things are basically as you said, young lady.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Those monsters are camped outside the city, and they've been destroying all our trade routes.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: We have limited reserves within the city, so if this continues, we're all going to be in big trouble.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Wait, you're saying no one has put a plan in place to distribute supplies or maintain order?

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Hah, we could all starve, and those nobles in the palace wouldn't even break a sweat.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Who knows? Maybe they've been in cahoots with the monsters all along.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That is concerning...

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Alright, alright, that's all the information you need, right? Off with you, now. I've still got business to do...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You know, if you smiled a little more, you'd definitely get more business, and I bet that would make your life just a little bit sweeter! I'm not saying it's guaranteed to work. It's just a tip!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Okay, while everyone is talking, I secretly use my magic props to summon a bottle of wine without the merchant noticing.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We meant no offense, sir. Here, allow me to offer you this bottle of vintage wine, made only from the finest grapes. I'll just leave it here. Please, enjoy it at your leisure.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ah, I should mention that this wine is the perfect accompaniment to a meal. I'd suggest enjoying it with dinner.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Hmm... Hmph, alright. Go on and ask. What do you want to know?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Do you have any information on the monsters, or the crisis that has overtaken the kingdom?

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Crisis? Ha, if you ask me, there's a crisis everywhere you look.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Those monsters are camped outside the city, and they've been destroying all our trade routes.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: We have limited reserves within the city, so if this continues, we're all going to be in big trouble.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Wait, you're saying no one has put a plan in place to distribute supplies or maintain order?

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Hah, we could all starve, and those nobles in the palace wouldn't even break a sweat.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Who knows? Maybe they've been in cahoots with the monsters all along.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That is concerning...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Thank you, sir. We won't take up any more of your time, now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, why did you leave in such a hurry?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Weeeell, you see, that bottle of "wine" was just a cardboard prop.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (A performance? I've never played a roleplaying game like this before, but even I can tell that suggestion is pretty far-fetched. Is a performance check really going to help here?)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Um... Alright. Ahem...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: By the harbor's grace, a lone boat lies in rest, let the moon give chase, for here begins our quest.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: In the dark of shadow, our heroes seek to find, where creatures born of evil, weave their grand design.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Blocked the road does stand, such is our hunters' plight, yet with sword and courage in hand, they march forth to pierce the night.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Hmph, I don't recall asking for a bardic song. Don't expect me to give you any coin.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: But if you meant what you sang, and you are indeed some kind of hunter... Then by all means, please go out, and kill those monsters for us.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Those monsters are camped outside the city, and they've been destroying all our trade routes.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: We have limited reserves within the city, so if this continues, we're all going to be in big trouble.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Wait, you're saying no one has put a plan in place to distribute supplies or maintain order?

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Hah, we could all starve, and those nobles in the palace wouldn't even break a sweat.

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Who knows? Maybe they've been in cahoots with the monsters all along.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That is concerning...

response.speaker: Gruff Merchant
response.text: Alright, I think I've said more than enough. Be on your way, now.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...Got it. Thank you, sir.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't mind him, Furina. He just doesn't have enough taste to appreciate your art.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh, no, I was just thinking about... how those nobles must be so cold-hearted. It's like they don't care about their people at all!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: With some suspicion, the captain allows you to survey his condition after you announce yourself as a trained doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, you're unable to adequately assess the source of his injury, much less come up with a way to relieve his pain.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... My skills are a little rusty.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Well, this is no ordinary wound... it was inflicted by a monster. Now, tell me, are you truly... a Marechaussee Hunter?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He regards you with suspicion for quite some time, before shaking his head. Perhaps he's finally accepted that you're here to help.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Sir, we were indeed in the city earlier, but our purpose was only to gather information on the monsters. We're here to help this city and all the people within it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Your guards are still fighting the monsters as we speak. They could be seriously wounded and in grave need of support. You need all the help you can get!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The man regards you with doubt and concern. After a period of inner struggle, he lets out a long sigh, and informs you of the locations where the monsters have appeared.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Some of our new recruits have never even dealt with a petty thief, and now they're out there fighting monsters... *sigh* If it weren't for this cursed leg...!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Please, sir, don't get too worked up. You need to focus on your recovery. Just leave the monsters to us — we're Marechaussee Hunters, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Hearing you say that, a glimmer of hope flashes in his eyes. But, it disappears almost as quickly as it came.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Those monsters aren't easy to deal with. But... if you insist on going, I won't stop you, either.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I just hope all the guards will be able to come back to their families alive. I wish you the best of luck...

talks.objective: Gather information at the central square of the capital

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He doesn't seem to notice your approach. Still immersed in his own thoughts, he shakes his head and lets out a long sigh.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (This guy seems promising enough. Maybe I can get some information out of him!)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hello, sir! Is there anything I can do to help you?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Wait, you're...!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Erm, I'm...

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Oh, dear goodness, you're... you're a Marechaussee Hunter!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You recognize us? Ah, are you... one of the people who wrote the commission letter?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Yes, yes! I didn't expect you to actually come. What great news... The city is saved!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: What happened here?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Alas... We once lived comfortable, carefree lives. This city used to be free of monsters. The first Marechaussee Hunter, Cassiodor, the "Golden Hunter," he was the one who drove them back.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: However... Monsters have once again surrounded the city. Perhaps the seal that kept them at bay has lost its power, or perhaps an evil sorcerer has been meddling in our affairs. All I know for sure is that their return has stripped this city of any chance at peace.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Are there... not enough soldiers to drive them out?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: It's not a question of numbers. The guards simply have no idea how to deal with them.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Most people my age have never even seen one of the monsters, much less been trained to fight against them. What's worse, many of us don't even know the history of the Marechaussee Hunters anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: When I was a child, though, my grandfather would tell me stories about how the Marechaussee Hunters drove back the monsters. So, on the off-chance that something might come of it, I decided to reach out to you.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: To be perfectly honest, I was starting to think all those stories were just tall tales, but now that I've seen you in person, I finally know that it was true!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, you can rest easy, friend! The righteous and formidable Marechaussee Hunters are on the case!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The man is touched by your determination and resolve. His eyes begin to well with tears of relief.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Still, if we're going to hunt the monsters, we need to know where to find them. Can you give us any leads?

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: All I know is that the area outside the city is dangerous. I'm afraid I can't point you toward a specific location.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Although, if you leave the capital through the main gate and follow the road, you should run into a group of guards. They might know more about where to find the monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I see... We'll go look for them, then.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Alright, be careful. Oh and... one last thing. The monsters outside the city are just part of the problem. There are evil sorcerers inside the city as well, so be on your guard.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: They're actively working with the monsters, and have corrupted the court ministers with malicious magic. They're the reason why, even inside the city, everything has been a giant mess.

dialogues.speaker: Anxious Man
dialogues.text: Even one of our kindest ministers has turned into a boorish and unreasonable figure, interested in nothing but enacting laws that exploit the people. Who knows how much longer we'll be able to go on like this...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Talk about being stuck between a rock and a hard place...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I feel bad for him. Maybe we should try to cheer him up?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hey, not everything can be solved with food!

response.speaker: Anxious Man
response.text: I appreciate your kindness, but for now, it's more important to focus on the crisis at hand.

response.speaker: Anxious Man
response.text: Brave Hunters, I leave the future of this kingdom to you.

choices.text: Furina could sing him a song?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Huh? Like... now? Is this really the right time...?

talks.objective: Discuss the information you have with the others
Discuss the information you have with the others

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: If I understood correctly, there are currently two problems in the kingdom that need solving, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Exactly. We need to defeat the monsters outside the city and take down the evil sorcerers stirring up trouble from within.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But, which problem should we tackle first...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Well, this seems like a good moment for a break. Take some time, and discuss what you want to do. Let me know when you've made your decision.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh... I really didn't expect the people in the city to keep us at arm's length like that. I totally thought the Hunters would be treated like heroes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Clorinde said the script took cues from the real history of Fontaine, right? Maybe the real-life Marechaussee Hunters were also treated like that?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I wouldn't say it's a perfect representation of history, but there are definitely some similarities. Would you like to hear more about it?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Sure, as long as it doesn't spoil anything in the script! You've brought up bits and pieces of the Hunters' history before, but it was all in passing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants to know, too! The Hunters were super powerful, right? Were they all from a special line of supernatural beings or something? Kinda like... the youkai in Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: No, all Marechaussee Hunters were ordinary mortal fighters. The only thing that set them apart were the special sword techniques passed down over the centuries.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So you mean... anyone could become a Marechaussee Hunter?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: In theory, yes. All you would need to do is survive the rigorous training, and master the swordsmanship techniques required to fight the monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Still, most people dropped out at the early stages, and others called it quits the minute they saw a monster in person. To become a Hunter, you must be strong in both body and mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What kind of monsters did the Hunters fight exactly? Oh and, the "evil sorcerer" the script mentions — did they exist in real life, too?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: The land of Fontaine once played host to an ancient dynasty known as Remuria. After that dynasty fell, monsters began to appear, intent on obstructing humans from establishing a new social order.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: One of the ancient sorcerers of Remuria used his power to assemble a formidable army of golems. He sought to use that force to establish himself as king.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Now wait a second! Don't tell me that guy was the inspiration for the evil sorcerer in the script! We still haven't found any in-game information on him yet, so why don't you talk about someone else for now?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Well, I wasn't planning on going into anything you might be able to find out in the game... But, if you want me to talk about something else, then... How about Cassiodor, the Golden Hunter, or Egeria, the ex-Hydro Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but those people are all from a super long time ago! Where did you learn all this, Clorinde?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: From my master.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: By "master," you mean... Ms. Petronilla?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Someone you know?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Absolutely. Ms. Petronilla and my father were good friends. Back in the day, she would often bring Clorinde over to play. But then...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...Let's not get off topic. Anyway, back to what I was saying...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Responding to Egeria's call, a number of warriors followed Cassiodor into battle against the monsters. This group of warriors, under Cassiodor's leadership, became known as the Marechaussee Hunters.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Yet, as Fontaine entered an era of peace, their work gradually became obsolete. The Marechaussee Phantom, originally an association made up of Hunters, eventually came to be predominantly comprised of Melusines.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ah, I see... That explains why most of the people in the script have forgotten the Hunters or think of them as nothing more than a legend.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Is that really a bad thing, though? It can get tough always being the one shouldering everyone's expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hmm, depends on who you ask, I suppose. If the name of the organization no longer commands respect, investigative work is bound to suffer.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Speaking of investigations, which problem should we tackle first? Monsters, or evil sorcerer?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I vote monsters. That's the main duty of the Hunters, right? We can come back to the sorcerer later.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well said, Miss Furina. Plus, if the sorcerer really are the masterminds behind this whole thing, defeating the monsters could give us some clues on their intentions as well.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What about you, partner? What do you think?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's decided, then!

response.speaker: Game Master
response.text: Alright, after some discussion, you decide to turn around and head out of the city...

choices.text: The sorcerer problem seems pretty important...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I mean... you're not wrong. But, those characters are usually the ones pulling the strings behind the scenes. More often than not, they're very formidable opponents. Going after them now might be jumping the gun a little bit.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We don't want a total party kill on the first day, right? With Clorinde as the GM, I wouldn't rule out the possibility...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...You've "persuaded" me.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, then it's settled! Let's go hunt some monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's take a look around, like that guy said...
You there! Outsiders! Halt!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Wh—Who's there?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: An armored man approaches you. He has a tall, muscular build and a determined expression in his eyes. Just one look, and you can tell he's fought in his fair share of battles.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Although he's trying his best to conceal his current state, his uneven gait and the sweat dripping down his forehead make it obvious that he's been wounded and is in serious pain.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I'm the captain of the guard. I saw you sneaking around the city earlier, so I'll only ask this once...

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: State your purpose, or it's off to the dungeons for the lot of you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's been a while since someone's been this suspicious of us...

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I said talk! Not whisper between yourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Er... Have you ever heard of the Marechaussee Hunters?

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Marechaussee Hunters? Hah, that fairy tale, you mean? What, you expect me to believe you're one of them?

talks.objective: Head to the depths of the forest

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to do a medicine check to see if I can help him...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to do an insight check to tell what he's thinking...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: While everyone is talking, you begin to carefully observe the captain's mannerisms.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Every so often, you see him glance toward a particular direction with a pained expression on his face, as if an invisible thread is tying him to an unknown place.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you follow his gaze, you vaguely recall that the location he seems fixated on is known for its difficult terrain. Any battle that breaks out in a place like that is likely to be prolonged and devastating.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that where the monsters are? Outside the forest, in the area with the difficult terrain?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The captain is taken aback by your sudden question. Still, his shock only lends credence to your theory.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: You're... looking to fight the monsters?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, we're Marechaussee Hunters, after all. You could say that's basically our job!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He shakes his head and continues to regard you with skepticism. In the end, he decides to inform you of the locations where the monsters have appeared.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Those monsters aren't easy to deal with. But... if you insist on going, I won't stop you, either.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I just hope all the guards will be able to come back to their families alive. I wish you the best of luck...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're counting on you, Navia!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Sir, we were indeed in the city earlier, but our purpose was only to gather information on the monsters. We're here to help this city and all the people within it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Your guards are still fighting the monsters as we speak. They could be seriously wounded and in grave need of support. You need all the help you can get!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The man regards you with doubt and concern. After a period of inner struggle, he lets out a long sigh, and informs you of the locations where the monsters have appeared.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Those monsters aren't easy to deal with. But... if you insist on going, I won't stop you, either.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I just hope all the guards will be able to come back to their families alive. I wish you the best of luck...

talks.objective: Go to the area where the monsters have appeared

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We used to be doctors.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've been studying medicine ever since I was a child. I want to do my part to eradicate these monsters and use what I've learned to heal others.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Welcome, welcome! When we face the monsters, I'll make sure to charge in front to give everyone some cover. You can take care of the healing at the back!

talks.objective: Go to the area where the monsters have appeared

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the place he mentioned... right?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You see broken iron swords scattered all around you and downed trees riddled with terrifying claw marks.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: All the signs point to one thing — a truly devastating battle just took place here.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Be on your guard, everyone. The monsters might still be around...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Before you can finish your sentence, you hear rustling sounds from the surrounding bushes. The monsters have emerged.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: They close in on you without fear. You get the impression that, in their bloodthirsty eyes, you're just another meal for them to devour.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Argh! L—Little help here! This thing wants to eat Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Your battle round begins... now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to do an insight check to tell what he's thinking...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Those monsters aren't easy to deal with. But... if you insist on going, I won't stop you, either.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I just hope all the guards will be able to come back to their families alive. I wish you the best of luck...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We used to be chefs.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've been studying the culinary arts since I was a child. I hope my delicious food can help boost people's spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: That's wonderful. I'll be looking forward to your cooking during our adventures together.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, if we're all here for the same commission, why don't we take some time to confirm what we need to do?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The monsters let out a terrifying roar of anger and resentment, before dissipating into thin air.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Phew... Thank goodness it's over!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We're lucky the Marechaussee Hunter class came with all those preset skill points. Otherwise, we would've been in some real trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I never knew the Fateometer even determines the amount of damage you inflict... If you get unlucky, isn't it just game over right then and there?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's part of the fun! The uncertainty of fate is what gives these games their appeal.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Just as you begin to celebrate your victory, a suspicious lump on the ground catches your attention.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A suspicious... lump? Wait, could it be... the thing that appears after every battle...!?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I walk up to it, crouch down, and begin to carefully examine it. I've still got my right glove on, so it should be fine for me to touch it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you investigate the mound, you discover that the exposed portion appears to be made of wood. It was previously obscured by the large form of the monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: With the monsters gone, the small protrusion now awaits your discovery, poking out of the ground like a shy flower bud.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah! It's a treasure chest!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's dig it up!

talks.objective: Discuss the information you have with the others
Discuss the information you have with the others

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: With everyone's help, you successfully excavate the wooden chest from the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Even without opening it, you can tell from the mora and jewels scattered around the chest that it must contain quite the fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Makes sense! We worked hard for this! Let's open it, and we can share what's inside!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha, I can understand your excitement, Paimon, but think about it... Doesn't it seem like there are people out there who need this treasure more than us?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah! Think about all the people suffering in the capital or all those guards who got hurt fighting the monsters... Wouldn't it be better if we gave the treasure to them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is that how it works? Paimon thought, since we were the ones to dig it up, we could just take it for ourselves...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, let's put it this way... Any decision you make during a roleplaying game can impact the future course of the story.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But, would the people really believe us? It's hard enough for us to prove we're Marechaussee Hunters. What if they think we procured the treasure illegally? They might get even more suspicious of us...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's definitely something we should consider. Maybe we can come up with an explanation in advance...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if donating it could cause that much trouble, why don't we use it to buy some gear and fill up on good food? Then, we'll be ready to fight even more bad guys!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Looks like you're facing a difficult choice once again.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Well, it's getting late. Why don't we call it a day for now.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Wow, where did the time go...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm not sure if it's because I'm having so much fun with you all, or because the story is particularly enticing... But, I feel like I could almost keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hear, hear! Ooh, how about we play through the night!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh!? Oh, um... I'm not sure I'll have enough energy for that...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yeah, that won't work for me, either. Lynette will give me an earful if I get home too late.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I understand how you feel, Navia, but we have to change venues for the next part of the story, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? Another location?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Mhm. There's a special note for the GM at the end of this section that says to proceed to an indoor set for the next part of the script.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Woah, they really pulled out all the stops for this new script!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, even if we end the game for the day, we can still stay a little longer and hear Clorinde finish her story, right? Paimon wants to hear more about the history of the Hunters...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmm, something tells me you just want to finish the free desserts before we break for the day...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—That's just a coincidence, okay? Besides, to Paimon, not finishing free food feels even worse than having to buy her own!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And anyway, Paimon really does want to hear more about Clorinde's master!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well...

choices.text: If the story doesn't have a happy ending...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: It's nothing. I appreciate the concern, but it's all in the past. It won't do any harm to share these things now.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: My earliest memories are of living with Master. According to her, she saved me from certain people of ill repute. My birth parents had left me behind some time before that.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (What a heavy beginning for a life story...)

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Master was a fascinating individual, if... inexperienced in the ways of raising children.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: My first ever toy was a short sword. Although, I suppose it wasn't so much a toy as something Master removed from her waist and handed to a noisy child in need of distraction.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Wait, so she... handed an actual sword to a child? Isn't that dangerous!? Did you hurt yourself?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Of course I did. I cut my palm, and bled quite a lot. But Master was not concerned. She just stood there and casually lectured me about it—

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: "See? That's what you get for not holding the sword properly," she told me. She then crouched down next to me and said, "Give me your hand. I'll teach you to bandage this wound. After that, it's time to learn how to truly hold a blade."

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Excuse me for asking this, Clorinde, but... how old were you, exactly, when all of this happened?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Probably around... three? Give or take.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Three!? Isn't that when most kids are still struggling to hold a fork?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: As I said, Master was... rather inexperienced in the ways of raising children. She believed trial and error was the best way to teach a child what they're capable of.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: (I'm not so sure this is a question of "experience"...)

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I didn't see anything wrong with her ways at the time, and, anyway, children don't get to choose how they're raised... Oh, she did bring me back a pet from Liyue once. It was a Geovishap Hatchling.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Geovishap Hatchling!? For a pet!? That seems even more dangerous!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: What she said was this — "Make sure to get along, you two. If you really can't agree on something, just settle it with a fight. Whoever loses is the real pet."

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Uh... And how old were you when this happened?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Five.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well... Did you win?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: No, I lost.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're saying... You actually became... the Geovishap's pet?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Yes, but only for a week. By the end of that week, I defeated it in combat, and we've shared a cordial relationship ever since.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (That really doesn't sound like the kind of childhood someone should have...)

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Later on, I gradually understood that Master most likely didn't know any other way to raise a child. She was a Marechaussee Hunter, but I never heard her bring up her own parents.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Thanks to her, I learned how to navigate the forest by the age of six, and could hunt monsters in the wild by myself the year after that.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Even though the training she subjected me to was strict, she always made sure to take me traveling when she had the time. We met many of her friends during those days... That was also how I met Mr. Callas and his family.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I still remember the first time we met. You were too scared to join our picnic and hid behind Ms. Petronilla the whole time.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I still... hadn't really met many children my age at that time, so I didn't know how to interact with others.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: After that, though, you started coming over a lot. You loved challenging people to shooting competitions, remember? I don't think many members of the Spina ever beat you in one of those.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I had a lot of fun during those days.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, I enjoyed them too! Oh, do you remember that one time we went exploring around the Spina together? We overheard Papa call your Master Fontaine's "Protector of Justice."

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We tried to pretend like we never heard anything, but you nearly let it slip that one time, hahaha...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: "Protector of Justice"? Wait, you mean... that vigilante hero from twenty years ago? The one who was always active at night?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Yep, that would be her. She would often put on a black cloak and go out at night. I never knew where she went or what she was doing... until, like Navia said, we overheard the truth from Mr. Callas that night.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Twenty years ago, huh... I still remember the Gardes leaving all kinds of witness reports about her on Neuvillette's desk.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: My apologies.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh... There's no need to apologize! You had nothing to do with it. And, anyway, everything she did was for a good cause.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Although, calling herself the "Protector of Order" was a bit much, especially when she deliberately operated outside the law...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? When did the "Protector of Justice" become the "Protector of Order"?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh, she had a bunch of codenames. I heard she would just come up with a name on the spot whenever she was asked...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Later on, she probably got sick of answering those questions and decided to stick to just two — the "Protector of Justice" and the "Protector of Order."

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: That sounds like her, all right. I bet she forgot which of the two she'd used by the time she got back each night.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, she certainly sounds like a fascinating individual. With her strong sense of justice, it's no surprise her student followed in her footsteps.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: It's true. I always wanted to become like her. Someone powerful, independent, and with a strong sense of conviction... But...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But...?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: ...She suddenly disappeared the night I turned ten years old.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Disappeared!? What happened?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I have no idea. She didn't even leave a note. I was never able to find out where she went.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: That night, I was celebrating my birthday at Navia's house, but Master never came to pick me up. When I returned home on my own, it was to an empty house.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: When she still didn't appear after a few days, I went to Mr. Callas' house to ask about her whereabouts, but he only shook his head.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Papa probably didn't know, either. I know he sent a few people to investigate the matter in secret, but... they never found any credible leads.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Don't worry, I understand. To be perfectly honest, given Master's personality and way of doing things, it all made a lot of sense. If I had to guess, I'd say she probably used it as an opportunity to force me to become independent.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Just like how... when a litter of kittens reaches a certain age, the mother willingly leaves them behind.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Were... Were you upset, Clorinde?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I was at first, but not anymore. I don't believe Master would suddenly disappear for no reason. There must have been something she just had to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, despite everything, you still managed to follow in her footsteps and become the greatest Champion Duelist in all of Fontaine! You're practically a living symbol of law and justice!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Hmm, I suspect my position would be far too "by-the-books" for her. Master always did whatever she pleased. But... you're right. I suppose I do take after her in some ways.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (Who knew Clorinde had such an interesting past... I never had the chance to ask her about it before.)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (I wonder... If Clorinde's master were the Champion Duelist back then... Would that duel against Mr. Callas have gone differently?)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (Oh no... Judging by the atmosphere, Clorinde and Navia are probably thinking something similar. The mood just got super awkward all of a sudden...)

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, anyway! Would you look at the time? It's getting dark, so we should probably call it a day for real this time. If we keep talking like this, we really will be here all night!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I had a great time today, Miss Clorinde. Thank you for being our GM.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Anytime.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: The script was good, but I've got to say, your childhood stories were even better!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hey, you should tell us more about that fight against the Geovishap some time! Maybe your master was onto something, hehe!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Hm, you could be right.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (What does she mean, "onto something"? I certainly don't know any five-year-olds who want to fight a vishap in their spare time!)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Guess I'll head back as well. I need to save my energy if I want to continue enjoying the story tomorrow.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: You're that excited to hear about my fight with the vishap?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I was talking about the script!

choices.text: It's okay not to finish it...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Whoa! They really have thought of everything. Even the Fateometer is here and ready to go for us!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...The Fateometer? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It's a card that's used to determine action success or failure. We'll need to use it when we try to use certain skills.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And what about all the dessert and tea? Is that for us as well?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: That's what the message said.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Really? That's so nice... It feels just like a tea party with friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those snacks have Paimon's name written all over them!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha, I think you might be more of a "Snack Hunter" than a Marechaussee Hunter, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Snack Hunter Paimon, reporting for duty! If there are delicious snacks to be found, Paimon'll track down every last one!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The desserts are great, but I'm still looking forward to the story more than anything.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Very fair. Then let us begin.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: First, please pick up the blank character cards in front of you, and write down your name and profession.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You can find an abbreviated version of the rules printed on the back of your character card. If you have any questions, feel free to ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: In this story, everyone is a Marechaussee Hunter. To reflect this, the club has prepared a small badge for everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Nice!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: As Hunters, you have proficiency in swordsmanship and fighting by default, so there's no need to allocate any additional skill points to those areas.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Swordsmanship? So there's a fighting part to all of this? Umm... Paimon's not sure she can do all that on her own. Maybe Paimon can just stick with you?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: #Why don't you share a character card, then? {NICKNAME} will be the Marechaussee Hunter and you can be {M#his}{F#her} little floating assistant.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hahaha, kinda like in real life.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So, for the name... Do I fill it out with the name of my character?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Yep. It can be any name you like.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You can use your real name too, if you want. I do that whenever I get too lazy to think of a new name.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh! So, it would be like... like experiencing a different life, but still as yourself? That's not a bad idea.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hmm, in that case... I think I'll continue to use the name "Lyney," then.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Next up is the skill sheet. You have a limited amount of skill points that you can use to learn a number of skills. The more points you invest in a particular skill, the easier it will be to pass associated checks.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm, I'll take "persuasion" and "investigation"! Those are must-haves when it comes to missions like these.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, those skills sound like they'd be useful for gathering intelligence. Good idea Navia! Just as expected of a veteran player!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmm... So should we also take those skills, then?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Not necessarily. Since we're working together as a team, we could leave the negotiations to Navia, and use our skill points to pick up other useful skills.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: For example... I think I'll take "stealth" and "sleight of hand." That will give us more options if we run into any situations we can't negotiate our way out of.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, interesting! I wasn't thinking about it like that. I suppose it's not so different from an acting troupe, everyone has their own role to play.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Let me see... I'll take "arts" and "performance." I'm not quite sure what use they'll be, but I'm not as knowledgeable about the other skills, and I'm not too confident I'd be able to roleplay them well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, that leaves us! What do you want to learn, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, something that will help you get a read on other people's thoughts! Sounds useful!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, so you want to help people when they're injured? That's nice of you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what do you think? Are you sure you want to learn these two skills?

choices.text: Let me think about this some more...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure. What do you want to learn?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, gotta say, this suits you really well! Nothing boosts morale like good food!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, so you want to help people when they're injured? That's nice of you!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Some time later, as a member of the Marechaussee Hunters, you receive a commission. Following the address provided on the message, you take a boat and arrive at this strange city.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you inhale, you can taste the slightly salty air of the docks as you begin to survey your surroundings. There aren't many people in the vicinity, but you do take note of a few others who, like you, seem to be sizing up this place.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Your eyes meet, and you realize these people are fellow Marechaussee Hunters, likely led to this location after receiving the same commission as you.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You're all Marechaussee Hunters too, right? Allow me to introduce myself! The name's Navia — monster hunter by trade and helpful neighborhood businesswoman on the side.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What say you to traveling together? We can help each other out on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Okay! Count me in.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: My name is Lyney. I've been wandering since I was little, and picked up a few less than legal tricks along the way. I was adopted by a Marechaussee Hunter and, later, chose to follow in his footsteps.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Is this where you introduce your character to everyone? It sounds like they've done this dozens of times.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: My name is Furina, and um... I grew up in a noble family. I always had a strong interest in performance and the arts. Even though I'm a Marechaussee Hunter, what I really want is to be a performing artiste...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey, that's really cool!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (You can do it, Furina! That's exactly how it's done!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon is Paimon, a good friend and companion to this Marechaussee Hunter right here!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Greetings, friend! Lovely weather we're having today, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Oh, hello... I suppose you're right. The weather today is quite lovely. If only those monsters out there would stop causing trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (It seems like every character included in the script has a certain amount of useful information to offer. If we keep asking questions, we might be able to get some good leads.)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Come now, don't be sad! Life is all about optimism! Oh, that reminds me, what did you have for breakfast this morning?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Uh... I don't think that's the kind of question we're supposed to ask...)

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Nothing turns a frown upside down like good food! How about some Macarons? I could make you some!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (...You didn't even take cooking as one of your skill proficiencies!)

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Ah... That's not necessary, Miss. Excuse me for saying this, but you don't really look like a chef. Besides, I'm not really a fan of sweets...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So you're someone who barely smiles and doesn't like sweets... Huh, you're really starting to remind me of this one friend of mine...

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Tch...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey, did she just "tch" me?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Clorinde must have broke character for a second!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #This isn't getting us anywhere... {NICKNAME}, maybe you can think of something?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Using your knowledge of medicine, you're able to deduce that the injury on his calf was a monster's doing, and the wound has already begun to fester. As you check him over, he looks at you with suspicion and retracts his injured leg further back.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm a doctor by trade — please let me redress your wound. You don't have to suffer like this.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The man appears somewhat disgruntled at having been exposed, but soon relents and raises his leg for you to take a better look.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He allows you to apply a poultice of specialized medicine to the wound, and it appears to bring him much relief. The tension in his brow eases.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Alright... Guess you lot might actually be real Marechaussee Hunters, after all. In any case, you've successfully treated my wound. So, what do you want to know?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you know where we can find the monsters? Or the other guards who are fighting them?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: He informs you of the various locations where monsters have appeared. He looks in that general direction with a pained gaze, as if a thin, invisible thread is pulling on his wound.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Some of our new recruits have never even dealt with a petty thief, and now they're out there fighting monsters... *sigh* If it weren't for this cursed leg...!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Please, sir, don't get too worked up. You need to focus on your recovery. Just leave the monsters to us — we're Marechaussee Hunters, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Hearing you say that, a glimmer of hope flashes in his eyes. But, it disappears almost as quickly as it came.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: Those monsters aren't easy to deal with. But... if you insist on going, I won't stop you, either.

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain
dialogues.text: I just hope all the guards will be able to come back to their families alive. I wish you the best of luck...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How about I cook something? Right here, right now!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: ...Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Positive!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: In that case, please refer to the Fateometer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it was a success!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You remain silent as you prepare a pot and fire to use for cooking. The woman stares at you with her mouth agape as you skillfully cut the ingredients and toss them into the pot.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: After some time, a rich aroma begins to fill the air. Even a passing cat can't help but stop in its tracks and look up in anticipation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please have some food. Who knows, maybe you'll feel better after eating something delicious?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Woah, that's amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Wait... So, as long as you pass the check, you can pretty much do anything, and it won't be seen as absurd?)

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Hah... You were right. This food really did make me feel better...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what had you so worried earlier? Could you tell us a bit more about it?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Okay, let me fill you in...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? We failed the check...

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You remain silent as you prepare a pot and fire to use for cooking. The woman stares at you with her mouth agape as you skillfully cut the ingredients and toss them into the pot.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Perhaps your skills have regressed due to lack of use, but, soon, the unpleasant smell of something burnt fills the air.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh no... I screwed it up.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's all black around the edges!

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: I appreciate the... thought, but I think I'll pass.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ahem... Miss, we'd love to learn more about the "monsters" you mentioned. If you're willing to open up to us, we might just be able to help resolve the troubles you're facing.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (You weren't even the one that learned "persuasion"...)

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: My troubles, you say... *sigh* I'm not sure they're so easily resolved, but I suppose it wouldn't hurt to share them with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: S—Seriously!?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: (Uh-oh! A critical failure!)

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You remain silent as you prepare a pot and fire to use for cooking. The woman stares at you with her mouth agape as you skillfully cut the ingredients and toss them into the pot.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Splash... Swoosh... Clang.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Clang!?

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You're unable to maintain control over the force of your stirring and accidentally knock over the entire pot. Hot soup spills all over the ground. You see evidence of your failed creation splattered on the surrounding furniture and across the hemline of the woman's skirt.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh no... I screwed it up.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: ...Excuse me. What is the meaning of this?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ahh, I'm so sorry!!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #{M#He}{F#She} just wanted to cook something delicious to cheer you up! {M#He}{F#She} really didn't do this on purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Is this situation salvageable at all?)

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Please, leave me be. I just want to be alone.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But, Miss...

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Please, don't force me to repeat myself.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ahahaha... Well, at least let us help clean up.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Critical failures are bound to happen... Don't be discouraged. Let's try and ask someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to do an insight check to see what's troubling her.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The results of insight checks aren't disclosed to the players, so I'll be the one consulting the Fateometer.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You recall all the lessons you've learned in your time and begin to carefully observe the woman's mannerisms.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You notice that when she's quiet, she has an empty look in her eyes, as if her thoughts have drifted to a place far, far away. And when she speaks, she often subconsciously reaches out to touch the ring on her left hand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did something happen to your husband?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Ah... So you noticed. That's a little embarrassing, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Um, any help here, Lyney?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Ahem... Miss, we'd love to learn more about the "monsters" you mentioned. If you're willing to open up to us, we might just be able to help resolve the troubles you're facing.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (You weren't even the one that learned "persuasion"...)

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: My troubles, you say... *sigh* I'm not sure they're so easily resolved, but I suppose it wouldn't hurt to share them with you.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: A horde of monsters suddenly appeared near the capital recently, so all the guards were dispatched to fight them.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Do you remember when those monsters appeared?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: ...I'm not completely sure. All I know is that my husband was dispatched to fight them three days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Do you know where he was sent?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: It all happened so fast. When we said our goodbyes, he couldn't even tell me where they were sending him.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You have our thanks, friend. We'll find and defeat those monsters as soon as possible. We sincerely hope your husband will be able to return to your side soon.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: Thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll find him! Just try to remain optimistic and wait for good news!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We don't always get to choose what happens to us, but we do get to choose the little things, like what we eat and how we respond to the things life throws our way. I hope that, one day, you too will recognize the power of something as small and inconsequential as a delicious dessert!

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Young Woman
dialogues.text: I... I'll do my best.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: You bid farewell to the woman and continue your journey further into the city.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you approach the tavern, you find a plainly-dressed woman standing nearby. She appears to be rather troubled about something.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you venture further into the city, the streets appear largely empty. An elderly woman walks past. You see her shake her head as she puts away her wrinkled wallet.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: A nearby merchant folds his arms and gives you a disdainful look. You get the impression that he's someone who has long gotten used to the sight before him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we try to go somewhere with more people?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ooh, how about the city square! Follow me!

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Before you lies the city's central square. You see a man with a slightly anxious look on his face pacing back and forth, his head hanging low.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Based on what the captain said, the monsters should be right up ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go. Hopefully we're not too late.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: As you approach the battlefield, you see numerous people lying by the side of the road. They appear to be dressed like guards.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: Their faces are filled with desperation and terror. Some are screaming and cursing in vain, as if still trying to banish the monstrosities they saw from their minds.

dialogues.speaker: Game Master
dialogues.text: The next battle round begins... now.
